mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (رسول): a badal (substitute) for (البينة), or nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of «هي رسول». (يتلو) is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (رسول). In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is (رسولا), in the accusative (naṣb), as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (فيها كتب): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of (صحف).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying (مخلصين) and (حنفاء): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent pronoun in (يعبدوا).
His saying (وذلك دين القيمة): (ذلك) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (دين) is the khabar (predicate) of (ذلك). (القيمة) is an adjective standing in place of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being «دين الملة القيمة», i.e. the upright (al-mustaqīma) [religion]; and it was said: its implied form is «دين الجماعة القيمة». His saying (والمشركين), the second one, is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (الذين); and it was said: it is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to (أهل), like the first, for the same reason. [Translator's note: the second (والمشركين) occurs in verse 6 of this surah, though the source treats it here.]

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying (جزاؤهم عند ربهم): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (جنات) is its khabar (predicate), i.e. their reward is entering gardens; (تجري) is a naʿt (adjective) of (جنات).
His saying (خالدين): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in (جزاؤهم). That is permissible because the maṣdar (verbal noun) here does not have the meaning of «أن فعل» and «أن يفعل», so as to require that nothing separate it from what is attached to it. Separation between it and what is attached to it is only prohibited when it has the meaning of «أن فعل» and «أن يفعل», and this is not of that kind. (أبدا) is an adverb of time.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (لم يكن الذين): the nūn was given kasra because it is vowelless and the lām after it is vowelless; its origin is vowellessness for the jussive. The wāw before it was dropped because it was vowelless and the nūn was vowelless, and the wāw was not restored when the nūn took a vowel, because the vowel is incidental and not taken into account. Its like is (قم الليل), and it is frequent in the Qur'an in every jussive or indeclinable verb whose middle radical is wāw or yāʾ, or an alif replacing one of them. Dropping the nūn from (يكن) here, according to the dialect of those who say (لم يك زيد قائما), is not good, because it has taken a vowel; it may be dropped only when it is vowelless in continuous speech, so that it resembles the letters of prolongation and softness and is dropped because of the resemblance and frequent use. When it takes a vowel, the resemblance disappears and dropping is prevented, except in poetry, for its dropping has come after it took a vowel because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.
His saying (والمشركين): conjoined to (أهل). It is not good to conjoin (المشركين) to (الذين), because the meaning would be reversed and the polytheists would become part of the People of the Book, while they are not of them.
His saying (منفكين): its meaning is "separating from one another", i.e. "divided"; what indicates that is His saying (وما تفرق الذين أوتوا الكتاب). It is taken from their saying "the thing has come apart (انفك) from the thing" when it separates from it. So it needs no khabar (predicate) when it means "divided"; had it meant "ceasing" it would have needed a khabar, because it would then be one of the sisters of (كان).
